question: The most frequent mechanism that induces the activation of the ABL protooncogene in chronic myeloid leukemia is:
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "Chronic myeloid leukemia" -> "BCR-ABL fusion protein" -> "translocation" -> "ABL protooncogene activation" -> 95%
CHAIN: "Chronic myeloid leukemia" -> "Philadelphia chromosome" -> "translocation" -> "ABL protooncogene activation" -> 93%
analysis: The ABL protooncogene is most frequently activated in chronic myeloid leukemia (CML) through a translocation event. This translocation, specifically the Philadelphia chromosome, involves the fusion of the BCR gene on chromosome 22 with the ABL gene on chromosome 9, creating the BCR-ABL fusion gene. This fusion gene encodes a constitutively active tyrosine kinase that drives the pathogenesis of CML.
